title: React Backend Integration Applied Check
description: Apply backend integration knowledge to REST status handling, authentication state, token refresh, multi-tab behavior, WebSocket cleanup, file upload cancellation, retries, and security mistakes.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A POST creates an order, the network times out, and the user clicks submit again. What backend-aware concern matters?

options.text: Duplicate creation; use idempotency keys or disable/reconcile repeated submits
Use array indexes as request ids

questions.explanation: Retries and repeated submits can duplicate non-idempotent operations unless the client and server design for idempotency or reconciliation.

questions.prompt: An API returns 401 for an expired access token. What is a typical refresh flow?

options.text: Try a controlled refresh, retry the original request if refresh succeeds, otherwise log out or ask the user to sign in

questions.explanation: A refresh flow should be bounded and explicit to avoid loops while preserving a valid session when possible.

questions.prompt: Which file upload practices are sound? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Validate file type and size on the server
Support cancellation or progress for large uploads when useful
Trust the browser `accept` attribute as the only validation

questions.explanation: Browser hints improve UX, but security and correctness require server-side validation. Large uploads may need progress and cancellation.

questions.prompt: A WebSocket connection is opened in `useEffect` but not closed on unmount. What problem can result?

options.text: Leaked connections and duplicate messages after remounts

questions.explanation: WebSocket effects need cleanup. Otherwise remounts can leave old connections active.

questions.prompt: If an app uses cookies for auth, CSRF considerations can still matter.
questions.explanation: Cookies may be sent automatically by the browser, so CSRF mitigations such as SameSite settings and CSRF tokens can be important.

questions.prompt: A user logs out in one tab but another tab still shows authenticated UI. What should the app consider?

options.text: Multi-tab session synchronization, such as storage events, BroadcastChannel, or server-driven invalidation
Using only CSS to hide auth state

questions.explanation: Auth state can become stale across tabs. Apps often coordinate logout or token changes across browser contexts.

questions.prompt: A retry strategy retries every failed request instantly forever. What is the main issue?

options.text: It can overload systems and create poor UX; use bounded retries and backoff for retryable failures

questions.explanation: Retries should distinguish retryable failures, limit attempts, and often use backoff or user-triggered retry.

questions.prompt: A React app hides an Admin button for non-admin users. What else is required?

options.text: The backend must still authorize admin API requests
Nothing; hidden buttons are complete security
The CSS class must be named `admin`
The token should be placed in the URL

questions.explanation: Client-side UI checks are not security boundaries. Attackers can call APIs directly, so server authorization is required.
